locations.quote: **Supervisors of theses spend considerable time on non-content-related feedback such as document structure, coherence, and linguistic accuracy. Much of this feedback is repetitive across students and disciplines, draining supervisors and leaving less capacity for substantive research discussions. For students, it translates into slower feedback turnaround. This thesis explores how large language models (LLMs) can generate formative feedback on theses and proposals based on supervisor-provided writing guidelines. Beyond a single draft, the tool also compares iterations to highlight improvements and surface persistent issues with more explanatory feedback. We evaluate single-prompt, prompt-chaining, and agentic setups, and assess trade-offs between local and cloud hosting. The tool integrates into Thesis Management, the thesis-lifecycle portal used by around 50 research groups at the Technical University of Munich, so supervisors can generate, revise, and publish feedback within their workflow.**
